name: PCI DSS v4.0 — Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard

articles.title: Install and maintain network security controls
articles.requirement: Network security controls (firewalls, cloud security groups) must be installed, configured, and maintained to protect the cardholder data environment.

articles.title: Processes and mechanisms for NSCs are defined and understood
articles.requirement: All security policies and operational procedures for managing network security controls are documented, kept up to date, in use, and known to all affected parties.

articles.title: Network security controls are configured and maintained
articles.requirement: NSC configurations restrict inbound and outbound traffic to that which is necessary, and all other traffic is specifically denied. Configurations are reviewed at least every six months.

articles.title: Network access to and from CDE is restricted
articles.requirement: Inbound traffic from untrusted networks is restricted to system components providing authorised public services. Direct connections between untrusted networks and the CDE are prohibited.

articles.title: Network connections between trusted and untrusted networks are controlled
articles.requirement: NSCs are implemented between all trusted and untrusted networks, including wireless networks, and controls prevent the forwarding of internal IP addresses.

articles.title: Risks to CDE from computing devices connecting to networks are mitigated
articles.requirement: Security controls are applied to any computing devices that connect to both untrusted networks and the CDE to prevent threats from being introduced.

articles.title: Apply secure configurations to all system components
articles.requirement: Vendor-supplied defaults and unnecessary services must be changed or removed before installing a system on the network.

articles.title: Processes for secure configurations are defined and understood
articles.requirement: Configuration standards are developed for all system components, address all known security vulnerabilities, and are consistent with industry-accepted hardening standards.

articles.title: System components are configured and managed securely
articles.requirement: Only necessary services, protocols, daemons, and functions are enabled. Security parameters are set to prevent misuse, and all unnecessary functionality is removed or disabled.

articles.title: Protect stored account data
articles.requirement: Stored account data must be protected using encryption, truncation, masking, hashing, or other methods to render it unreadable.

articles.title: Processes to protect stored account data are defined and understood
articles.requirement: Security policies for protecting stored account data are documented, kept up to date, and known to all affected parties.

articles.title: Sensitive authentication data is not stored after authorisation
articles.requirement: SAD (full track data, card verification codes, PINs) is not retained after authorisation, even if encrypted. Issuers may store SAD with business justification.

articles.title: Access to displays of full PAN is restricted
articles.requirement: PAN is masked when displayed, showing at most the first six and last four digits, with full PAN accessible only to those with a legitimate business need.

articles.title: PAN is secured wherever it is stored
articles.requirement: PAN is rendered unreadable anywhere it is stored using strong cryptography, one-way hashes, truncation, or index tokens with securely stored pads.

articles.title: Cryptographic keys used to protect stored account data are secured
articles.requirement: Key management processes and procedures for cryptographic keys used to protect stored cardholder data are defined, implemented, and documented.

articles.title: Protect cardholder data with strong cryptography during transmission
articles.requirement: Cardholder data must be encrypted with strong cryptography during transmission over open, public networks.

articles.title: PAN is protected with strong cryptography during transmission
articles.requirement: PAN is secured with strong cryptography whenever transmitted over any network. Only trusted keys and certificates are accepted.

articles.title: Protect all systems and networks from malicious software
articles.requirement: Anti-malware mechanisms must be deployed on all systems commonly affected by malicious software.

articles.title: Malicious software is prevented or detected and addressed
articles.requirement: An anti-malware solution is deployed on all system components except those identified as not at risk, performs periodic scans and active/real-time scanning.

articles.title: Anti-malware mechanisms and processes are active, maintained, and monitored
articles.requirement: Anti-malware solution must generate audit logs, is kept current with latest signatures, and cannot be disabled or altered by users without management authorisation.

articles.title: Anti-phishing mechanisms protect users
articles.requirement: Technical controls are in place to detect and protect personnel against phishing attacks, including email-based threats.

articles.title: Develop and maintain secure systems and software
articles.requirement: Security vulnerabilities must be identified and addressed through patching and secure software development practices.

articles.title: Bespoke and custom software is developed securely
articles.requirement: Software development is based on industry standards and/or best practices for secure development, software is reviewed prior to release, and development personnel are trained.

articles.title: Security vulnerabilities are identified and addressed
articles.requirement: All system components are protected from known vulnerabilities by installing applicable security patches within one month for critical and high vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Public-facing web applications are protected against attacks
articles.requirement: Public-facing web applications are protected against known attacks using web application firewalls or manual/automated vulnerability security assessment tools.

articles.title: Restrict access to system components and cardholder data by business need to know
articles.requirement: Access to system components and cardholder data must be limited to only those individuals whose job requires such access.

articles.title: Access to system components and data is appropriately defined and assigned
articles.requirement: Access control systems are configured to enforce need-to-know, with default deny-all setting and access granted only by explicit role-based authorisation.

articles.title: Access to system components and data is managed via an access control system
articles.requirement: Access is controlled by an automated access control system that restricts access based on business need and uses least privileges.

articles.title: Identify users and authenticate access to system components
articles.requirement: Every user must be assigned a unique identification to ensure actions are performed and tracked by known and authorised users.

articles.title: User identification and related accounts are strictly managed
articles.requirement: Shared/group/generic accounts are not used. User IDs and credentials are managed through their lifecycle. Inactive accounts are removed within 90 days.

articles.title: Strong authentication for users and administrators
articles.requirement: Multi-factor authentication is required for all access into the CDE. Passwords/passphrases require a minimum length of 12 characters (or 8 if system does not support 12).

articles.title: MFA is implemented to secure access into the CDE
articles.requirement: MFA is implemented for all non-console access into the CDE and for all remote network access originating from outside the entity's network.

articles.title: Use of application and system accounts is strictly managed
articles.requirement: Application and system accounts and related authentication factors are managed, with interactive login disabled where possible and passwords changed periodically.

articles.title: Restrict physical access to cardholder data
articles.requirement: Physical access to cardholder data or systems that store, process, or transmit cardholder data must be appropriately restricted.

articles.title: Physical access controls manage entry into facilities and systems
articles.requirement: Physical access to sensitive areas is controlled using appropriate entry controls such as badge readers, locks, and monitoring of physical access.

articles.title: Log and monitor all access to system components and cardholder data
articles.requirement: Logging mechanisms and the ability to track user activities must be implemented for all system components.

articles.title: Audit logs are implemented to support detection of anomalies
articles.requirement: Audit logs record all individual user access, actions taken by anyone with root/admin privileges, access to audit trails, invalid access attempts, and changes to authentication mechanisms.

articles.title: Audit logs are reviewed to identify anomalies or suspicious activity
articles.requirement: Audit logs are reviewed at least daily for security events and critical system alerts. All other logs are reviewed periodically per the entity's risk strategy.

articles.title: Test security of systems and networks regularly
articles.requirement: Security systems and processes must be tested regularly through vulnerability scans and penetration testing.

articles.title: External and internal vulnerabilities are regularly identified and addressed
articles.requirement: Internal vulnerability scans quarterly, external scans by ASV quarterly, and penetration testing at least annually and after significant changes.

articles.title: External and internal penetration testing is regularly performed
articles.requirement: Penetration testing is performed at least annually and after significant changes, covering the entire CDE perimeter and critical systems. Exploitable vulnerabilities are corrected and retested.

articles.title: Support information security with organisational policies and programmes
articles.requirement: A comprehensive information security policy must be established, published, maintained, and disseminated to all relevant personnel and vendors.

articles.title: Risks to the CDE are formally identified, evaluated, and managed
articles.requirement: A targeted risk analysis is performed for each PCI DSS requirement that specifies flexibility for how frequently the requirement is performed, and a formal risk assessment is performed at least annually.
